questions.title: Epstein-Barr virus is associated with nasopharyngeal carcinoma
questions.question: Epstein-Barr virus is associated with development of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Gastric carcinoma's characteristic infectious association is H. pylori, not EBV, in this teaching.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Oesophageal carcinoma is not the characteristic EBV-associated malignancy.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Laryngeal carcinoma is not the characteristic EBV-associated malignancy; it is more strongly linked to smoking and alcohol.
explanations.D: Correct. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is causally implicated in nasopharyngeal carcinoma, along with Burkitt's lymphoma, other B-cell lymphomas and some cases of Hodgkin lymphoma. EBV either integrates a viral oncogene into host DNA or produces proteins that inactivate tumor suppressor gene products, and nasopharyngeal carcinoma is one of its best-established malignant associations, distinct from gastric, oesophageal or laryngeal carcinoma.

questions.title: Tumor suppressor genes prevent malignant transformation
questions.question: Genes that function in a manner that prevents malignant transformation:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Proto-oncogenes are the normal, unmutated precursor genes that promote controlled cell growth; they do not themselves prevent malignant transformation, and become growth-promoting oncogenes only on gain-of-function mutation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Oncogenes actively promote autonomous cell growth once activated, the opposite of preventing malignant transformation.
explanations.C: Correct. Tumor suppressor genes -- "governors" such as RB, which restrain proliferation, and "guardians" such as TP53, which sense DNA damage -- function to prevent malignant transformation. Loss-of-function mutation of tumor suppressor genes removes this restraint, contributing to cancer development, in contrast to oncogenes, which actively drive it when activated.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Antiapoptotic genes promote cell survival by blocking programmed cell death; overactivity can contribute to cancer, so they do not function to prevent malignant transformation.

questions.title: Oncogenes promote autonomous cell growth in cancer cells
questions.question: Genes that promote autonomous cell growth in cancer cells are called:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Tumor suppressor genes restrain proliferation or sense DNA damage; they act to prevent, not promote, autonomous growth.
explanations.B: Incorrect. DNA repair genes maintain genomic integrity by correcting DNA damage; their loss increases mutation accumulation, but they are not themselves the genes that actively drive autonomous growth.
explanations.C: Correct. Oncogenes are genes that promote autonomous cell growth in cancer cells, arising when a normal proto-oncogene acquires a gain-of-function mutation. This drives uncontrolled proliferation independent of normal growth signals, the opposite role from tumor suppressor genes, which instead restrain proliferation or sense DNA damage.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Antiapoptotic genes block programmed cell death rather than directly promoting autonomous growth; this is a related but distinct mechanism from the one the printed key names.

questions.title: Aflatoxin from Aspergillus flavus causes liver cancer
questions.question: Toxic metabolites produced by the fungus Aspergillus flavus contaminating food stuffs are involvement in development of which of the following cancers?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Aflatoxin's carcinogenic target organ is the liver, not the uterus.
explanations.B: Correct. Aflatoxin, a chemical carcinogen produced by the fungus Aspergillus flavus contaminating grain and nut food stuffs, causes hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). This is a food-contaminant, not a synthetic industrial, chemical carcinogen, and its liver-specific target distinguishes it from the other options here.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Aflatoxin's carcinogenic target organ is the liver, not bone.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Aflatoxin's carcinogenic target organ is the liver, not skin; chronic UV exposure, not a fungal food contaminant, is the characteristic skin cancer risk factor.
